rows.question: On the Raspberry Pi 4B, how does the end-to-end latency of the radar-only model compare with the radar and vibration fusion model in the bathroom study?
rows.expected: Radar only 28.4 ms vs fusion 15.8 ms
rows.answer: On the Raspberry Pi 4B, the radar-only Motion-Mamba model has an end-to-end latency of 28.4 ms (7.5 ms preprocessing, 19.8 ms inference). [1] The radar and vibration fusion model has an end-to-end latency of 15.8 ms (8.9 ms preprocessing, 6.7 ms inference). rows.question: In the bathroom study, how much energy per 2.56 s window do the radar sensing node and the vibration sensing node use?
rows.expected: Radar node (ESP32-C3 + C4001) 4740 mJ; vibration node (ESP32-C3 + ADXL345) 820 mJ
rows.answer:
The paper does not report energy per 2.56 s window for the radar sensing node itself; the reported energy is measured on the Raspberry Pi 4B gateway, which performs the inference. [1][2] The radar node (C4001 with ESP32-C3) only does sensing, timestamping and lightweight preprocessing and then sends 2.56 s windows to the gateway. [2] The proposed fused model uses 10750 mJ per window on the gateway, versus 14200 mJ for the strongest baseline. [1] No separate energy figure is reported for the paper's own vibration node; only vibration-only baselines are given, using 12131 mJ (vibration rule), 14931 mJ (thresholded accelerometer) and 19210 mJ (ML wearable) per window.
